question: Did full-episode student roll-ins, rather than scheduled 64-action resets, change final-checkpoint agreement with the native replanned teacher on identical independent-map turn-start states?

data.teacher_label: First action of the selected three-turn whole-turn plan; the separate same-state cache audit found this first action identical for cached and replanned search on 2548/2548 states.

analysis: Replay each recorded root observation and legal-action order once per checkpoint, infer frozen source and both students with direct argmax, and count teacher-action matches, exact source corrections and off-target departures by seat, teacher action kind, legal-action count and independent map. Compare full episode against reset64 on the same maps; report exact two-sided map sign p without treating this retrospective sample as a promotion gate.
stop_rule: If any input hash, map count or legal teacher action differs, stop without substituting data. Do not train, select checkpoints, use this audit to tune on old windows, run reserved teacher/final games, rate or deploy either rejected student.
interpretation: These are post hoc first-action fidelity measurements on previously inspected fit maps, not terminal credit, later-turn fidelity, game strength, Elo or a causal explanation for the failed fresh complete-game gate.
resources: Read-only one pinned nice19 CPU on SSH server fedora-toolbox scratch; tiny JSON outputs, no GPU, no new maps or search.
